q: What is the minimum size of a refrigeration waste pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Refrigeration waste pipe sizes: 32 mm minimum; 51 mm for one inlet serving up to 2.8 m³; 76 mm for larger capacities with several 32 mm inlets.

q: For an island sink, how does the return vent connect to the horizontal drain?
o: Through a sanitary tee on its side
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The wye lets any water that runs into the foot vent drain back into the drain.

q: How is cooling water from equipment connected to a fixture trap?
o: Directly to the outlet side of the trap
Below the weir of the trap
To the trap inlet, 152 mm above the overflow rim
Straight to the building drain, with no trap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Discharging high above the rim keeps the water supply line from being submerged if the fixture backs up.

q: How does air-conditioning condensate drain?
o: Into the vent stack through a tee
Onto the roof deck, to evaporate
Through indirect waste to an approved receptor
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Approved points include a trapped receptor, a dry well, a leaching pit or a fixture tailpiece. An indirect connection discharges through an air gap or air break into a trapped receptor, so sewage can never back up into the equipment.

q: An island sink has its own special vent. What else may its drain serve?
o: Any fixture on the same floor
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The island venting method only works for the one fixture it was designed for.

q: What minimum thickness must a metal condenser or sump be?
o: No. 12 B&S gauge galvanized iron (about 2.77 mm)
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Condensers and sumps take hot water and steam, so they must be heavy enough not to corrode or buckle.

q: What is the minimum air gap for an indirect drainage connection?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: An indirect connection discharges through an air gap or air break into a trapped receptor, so sewage can never back up into the equipment.

q: In a combination waste-and-vent system, how large must the vent be?
o: At least 25% of the area of the drain
Equal to the area of the drain
At least 32 mm, whatever the drain size
At least 50% of the area of the drain it serves
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Combination waste-and-vent systems use oversized pipe so air can travel above the water. Branches over 4.6 m get their own vent.

q: May a chemical waste vent connect to the building's other vents?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Chemical fumes would corrode ordinary vents and escape through other fixtures.

q: May a vent from indirect waste piping be combined with other vents?
o: Yes, if sized up one pipe size
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Indirect waste is kept fully separate from the sanitary system, vents included.

q: In a combination waste-and-vent system, what vertical waste pipe is allowed?
o: Any vertical pipe up to 3.0 m
Only a vertical stack of any height
Only a fixture tailpiece, up to 0.60 m long
No vertical pipe at all, not even a tailpiece
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Vertical drops in a combination system fill the pipe and cut off the air path. Combination waste-and-vent systems use oversized pipe so air can travel above the water. Branches over 4.6 m get their own vent.

q: How many fixtures at most may be served by a wet-vented section?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Wet venting is limited so the flow never fills the pipe and blocks the air.

q: What strainer is used on a floor receptor that takes indirect waste?
o: A flat grate with fine holes
A basket strainer that stops all solids
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The raised beehive shape keeps debris from blocking the receptor.

q: How is a swimming pool pump's discharge connected to the drainage system?
o: Directly to the public water main
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: An air gap keeps sewage from ever siphoning back into the pool. An indirect connection discharges through an air gap or air break into a trapped receptor, so sewage can never back up into the equipment.

q: How high must the vent of an island sink rise?
o: Only up to the trap weir
At least 1.5 m above the floor
As high as possible, at least to drainboard height
Up to the ceiling above the island
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The vent rises inside the island cabinet, then loops down and back to the drain.

q: How do appliances such as dishwashers and ice makers drain?
o: Onto the floor, to a floor drain
Through indirect waste into open receptors
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: An indirect connection discharges through an air gap or air break into a trapped receptor, so sewage can never back up into the equipment.

q: What size of refrigeration waste pipe serves larger capacities with several 32 mm inlets?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Refrigeration waste pipe sizes: 32 mm minimum; 51 mm for one inlet serving up to 2.8 m³; 76 mm for larger capacities with several 32 mm inlets.

q: What slope must the vent line of an island sink have?
o: 10 mm per m (1%) away from the drain
20 mm per m (2%) toward the drain
40 mm per m (4%) away from the drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The foot vent must drain back into the waste pipe.

q: What water may NOT be discharged directly into the drainage system?
o: Water at 60°C or hotter, and steam
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Hot water and steam soften plastic pipe and damage joints. It must be cooled first, in a sump.

q: How is food-handling equipment separated from the drainage system?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Sewage backing up into food equipment would contaminate the food. The air gap makes that impossible.

q: In a combination waste-and-vent system, when must a branch be vented separately?
o: When it is longer than 4.6 m
When it is longer than 1.5 m
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Combination waste-and-vent systems use oversized pipe so air can travel above the water. Branches over 4.6 m get their own vent.

q: What must be done to chemical waste before it enters the drainage system?
o: It must be diluted with hot water
It must go straight to the public sewer
Nothing, if the pipe is PVC
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Pretreatment neutralizes acids and other chemicals. The facility must be approved.

q: Who must approve indirect waste arrangements?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The Plumbing Official checks that air gaps and receptors will work.

q: In a combination waste-and-vent system, how large are the waste pipe and each trap?
o: One pipe size larger than otherwise required
One pipe size smaller than usual
Two pipe sizes larger than otherwise required
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Combination waste-and-vent systems use oversized pipe so air can travel above the water. Branches over 4.6 m get their own vent.

q: Wet venting is limited to trap arms carrying how many fixture units?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Small flows leave room at the top of the pipe for air.

q: What receptor does a clothes washer drain into?
o: A floor drain with no trap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The standpipe rises above its trap so the washer's pump discharge cannot overflow.

q: How do clear-water wastes such as tank overflows and sprinkler drains discharge?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Clear water is not sewage, but its equipment must still be protected from backflow. An indirect connection discharges through an air gap or air break into a trapped receptor, so sewage can never back up into the equipment.

q: How is a common vent sized?
o: From the largest single fixture only
From the height of the building
From the sum of the fixture units it serves
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: A common vent serves two traps, so both loads count.

q: How does sterilizing equipment drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Hospitals cannot risk sewage entering sterile equipment.

q: What size of refrigeration waste pipe serves one inlet with a capacity up to 2.8 m³?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Refrigeration waste pipe sizes: 32 mm minimum; 51 mm for one inlet serving up to 2.8 m³; 76 mm for larger capacities with several 32 mm inlets.

q: For an island sink vent, what is the critical level?
o: At the level of the trap weir
At the level of the floor
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The vent must stay dry even if the sink fills to the rim.

q: How do drinking fountains drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Drinking fountains carry water that people drink, so they are kept apart from the drainage.

q: How do evaporative coolers and air washers drain?
o: Straight into the supply air duct
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Their drain water passes through an air break into a trapped receptor.

q: Where are cleanouts placed on an island sink's foot vent?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Waste can collect in the looped vent, so it must be cleanable.

q: How large must a boiler blow-off sump be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The sump cools the hot blow-down water before it enters the drainage system.

q: What minimum air gap protects a potable water outlet?
o: 25 mm, or twice the inlet pipe diameter
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The gap between the faucet and the flood rim stops backsiphonage into the water supply.

q: In a combination waste-and-vent system, where does the vent connect?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Combination waste-and-vent systems use oversized pipe so air can travel above the water. Branches over 4.6 m get their own vent.

q: May chemical waste be discharged to the ground?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Chemicals would poison soil and groundwater.

q: What must be provided at changes of direction in indirect waste piping?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Indirect waste lines are often long and small, so they must be cleanable at bends.

q: In a combination waste-and-vent system, when is no cleanout required at a fixture?
o: When the fixture is a water closet
When the branch is over 4.6 m
When the tailpiece is under 51 mm
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: Small tailpieces can be cleared from the fixture itself.

q: How large must a wet-vented section be?
o: One size larger than the upper fixture drain
The same size as the upper fixture drain
One size smaller than the upper fixture drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: The extra size keeps room for air above the water.

q: How must drains, overflows and relief outlets of the water supply system connect to sanitary drainage?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 8
n: A direct connection could let sewage into the water system.
